newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen falling slower next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen falling slower next week.

text.p: The Polish bourse is seen extending this week's fall next week as investors continue to take profits after the exchange's 38-percent rise from mid-December to mid-February.

Analysts said Friday's information of a deeper than expected slide in U.S. wholesale prices, which cheered some Western bourses in the view that U.S. rates would remain stable, could lead to growth in Warsaw on Monday.
But they said subsequent falls were still possible.
"I think a lot of investors got scared by the recent big falls and will use a possible rebound to take profits," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
The Warsaw bourse's main market tumbled 5.7 percent this week to 16,687.1 points.

Analysts said small-cap stocks were undergoing particularly sharp corrections after recent speculative surges, but that some large-cap stocks, which led the bull run earlier this year, still had downside potential.

"There's still plenty of room for falls, though they should be milder....There's no tragedy on the market and most investors should use the falls to change their portfolios," said Remigiusz Tarka, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.
Tarka said there were some fundamentally strong firms which needed 30 or 40 percent falls to become buys again.

Analysts also said some investors were saving their money for the forthcoming large public offerings of Agros and paper firm Celuloza Swiecie SA. From March 20 to 26 Agros is offering 2.43 million shares at between 65 and 80 zlotys.
Celuloza Swiecie's 7.5-million-share initial public offering, at a minimum price yet to be determined, takes place in mid-April.
Some analysts said firms' February earnings reports due early next week could help stem losses, especially if construction firms do well during this year's mild winter.
Analysts said the finance minister's statement this week that Monday's February inflation figure could be low enough to bring year-on-year inflation below 18 percent was a good sign.
They said his comment that the next interest rate move would likely be a cut also boded well, but that stocks might not be affected as the move was not expected until the third quarter.
Analysts said speculators would have more time to play on Espebepe, whose creditors decided to put off a decision on a possible debt write-off deal until April 14.
The stock led losers this week, falling 19.3 percent before its trade was suspended on Friday before the creditors met.
